title: Predicting What Matters: Robust Generalist Robot Policy Learning via Future Semantic Mask
claim: Predicting future semantic masks instead of pixels yields a robust end-to-end policy that outperforms RGB-based baselines.
layout: 3 zones, left-to-right: inputs, architecture diagram, stacked bar charts at right
description: A wide figure with three regions. The left blue panel shows multi-view observations (front and wrist camera images from LIBERO, RLBench and real-world) and a task prompt in a dashed speech bubble. The centre grey panel is the architecture. A VAE encodes the images into tokens. An interpolate-and-stack block merges these with noise and memory RGB tokens. A tall Future Mask DiT then feeds a Mask Decoder, which outputs colourful predicted semantic masks for the front and wrist views. A text encoder also feeds the DiT. An Action Expert, an Action Decoder and noised-action input produce the action outputs. Scissors icons mark random token pruning. The right panel has three bar charts for performance, robustness and OOD generalization, comparing Pi0, GE-ACT and MWM, with MWM's values highlighted in red.
caption: MWM overview. MWM learns a mask-centric predictive world model from semantic supervision during training, but runs purely on raw multi-view RGB at test time. Training proceeds in two stages: we first learn to forecast future semantic masks via conditional diffusion, then train a diffusion policy that conditions on mask-centric predictive features for action generation. This semantic bottleneck prioritizes decision-relevant geometry and interaction dynamics over photometric realism.
abstract: World models derived from large-scale video generative pre-training have emerged as a promising paradigm for generalist robot policy learning. However, standard approaches often focus on high-fidelity RGB video prediction, this can result in overfitting to irrelevant factors, such as dynamic backgrounds and illumination changes. These distractions reduce the model's ability to generalize, ultimately leading to unreliable and fragile control policies. To address this, we introduce the Mask World Model (MWM), which leverages video diffusion architectures to predict the evolution of semantic masks instead of pixels. This shift imposes a geometric information bottleneck, forcing the model to capture essential physical dynamics and contact relations while filtering out visual noise. We seamlessly integrate this mask dynamics backbone with a diffusion-based policy head to enable robust end-to-end control. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the superiority of MWM on the LIBERO and RLBench simulation benchmarks, significantly outperforming the state-of-the-art RGB-based world models. Furthermore, real-world experiments and robustness evaluation (via random token pruning) reveal that MWM exhibits superior generalization capabilities and robust resilience to texture information loss.
